name: The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel
positioning: Rosewood hotel on Manhattan's Upper East Side, first opened in 1930, home to Bemelmans Bar and Cafe Carlyle
best_for: Music lovers who want live piano, jazz and cabaret downstairs
Travelers who want a base around the corner from Central Park and close to the Met

facts.text: The hotel is on Manhattan's Upper East Side, right around the corner from Central Park.
Bemelmans Bar has nightly piano and late-night jazz.
At Bemelmans Bar, a cover charge applies from 5:30 pm, starting with the pianist's opening set, followed by a jazz trio from 9 pm.
Cafe Carlyle originally opened in 1955 and headlines performers in a classic cabaret setting.
Dowling's at The Carlyle serves modern interpretations of New York classics, set amid a collection of more than 200 works by local artists.
Guestrooms were decorated by designers including Tony Chi and Thierry Despont.
Suites sit above Madison Avenue and are furnished with original artwork.
Signature Suites come with the attentiveness of Suite Ambassadors.
Wellness includes a Valmont Spa for facials and body treatments, the Yves Durif Salon, and a fitness center with Technogym equipment and personal training.
Bemelmans Bar offers a private martini-making masterclass with its red-jacketed bartenders.
Hotel guests get priority when Bemelmans Bar seats walk-ins, so show your room key.

highlights.text: In 1947, Ludwig Bemelmans was commissioned to paint large-scale murals in Bemelmans Bar depicting all four seasons in nearby Central Park.
Cafe Carlyle is an intimate supper club set against Marcel Vertes' murals, with classic cabaret.
The Gallery, designed by decorator Renzo Mongiardino and inspired by Topkapi Palace, serves afternoon tea and light refreshments late into the night.
More than 20 suites have Steinway or Baldwin baby-grand pianos.
A town car is on hand to take guests anywhere within a 20-block radius.

considerations.text: Common areas are fairly minimal beyond some lobby seating and the dining venues.
Cafe Carlyle requires reservations and jackets, and the bars and restaurants ask guests not to wear athletic or casual wear.
There is a welcome amenity for children, but no formal kids club.
